summary:
Mars.loc - Making Mars Exploration Safer and Smarter 

Exploring Mars is one of humanity's greatest challenges. Its rocky landscapes, deep valleys, and unfamiliar terrain make navigation difficult for future astronauts. To address this challenge, our team, X-terrestrials, developed "Mars.loc" for the NASA International Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Mars.loc is an interactive Mars navigation platform designed to make exploring the Martian surface easier, safer, and more understandable. Our prototype features an interactive map that allows users to explore Mars, zoom into different areas, visualize a proposed travel route, and view important navigation information, including estimated travel duration.

Our project addresses the challenge by demonstrating how planetary mapping and route visualization can support future space exploration. Our vision is to develop intelligent navigation features that identify safer routes by analyzing terrain conditions, elevation changes, and potential hazards.

We also plan to integrate Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR) to create immersive navigation experiences, allowing astronauts to explore and understand Martian environments more effectively.

Mars.loc is important because future astronauts will need reliable navigation tools to explore unfamiliar environments. Our goal is to contribute to safer, smarter, and more efficient planetary exploration.

Mars.loc: Making the unknown easier to explore in the safest way possible.

Mars.loc – Project Details

Project Overview

Mars.loc is an interactive Mars navigation and terrain visualization platform developed by Team X-terrestrials for the NASA International Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our goal is to make exploring Mars safer, smarter, and more accessible by combining real planetary data, interactive mapping, and 3D visualization.

Our project demonstrates how future astronauts could explore unfamiliar Martian landscapes, examine potential routes, and access important navigation information through one user-friendly platform.

How Does Mars.loc Work?

Mars.loc is a web-based platform that allows users to explore the Martian surface through interactive maps and terrain visualizations.

Users can zoom in and out, examine different areas of Mars, view a predefined navigation route, and access information such as location details, time indicators, and estimated travel duration.

The platform uses real Mars imagery and elevation datasets from NASA, USGS, and Esri to represent the Martian environment.

Our project also incorporates data from NASA's Perseverance rover mission, including its route, elevation information, scientific stops, and surface photographs. These resources help connect our navigation concept with actual Mars exploration.

Technologies and Tools Used

We developed Mars.loc using modern web development technologies, mapping libraries, 3D graphics tools, and scientific data processing software.

Website Development

  • Next.js 16: The main framework used to build our web application.
  • React 19: Used to create the interactive user interface.
  • JavaScript and CSS: Used for website functionality, design, and styling.

Mapping and 3D Visualization

  • Leaflet: Used to create interactive 2D maps of the Martian surface.
  • Three.js: Used for 3D terrain visualization.

Data Processing

  • Python: Used to process and prepare planetary datasets.
  • NumPy: Used for numerical calculations.
  • Rasterio: Used to read and process terrain elevation and map files.
  • Pillow: Used for image processing.

Hosting and Deployment

  • GitHub: Used to manage the project's code.
  • Vercel: Used to deploy and host the website.

NASA Maps and Scientific Data Sources

Mars.loc uses planetary datasets and imagery to create a more realistic exploration experience.

  • MOLA: Elevation-based map tiles from NASA Mars Trek.
  • THEMIS: Thermal infrared map tiles from NASA Mars Trek.
  • CTX Imagery: Wider-area Martian surface images from Esri OnMars.
  • CTX Elevation Data: Terrain height information from USGS, supporting slope information outside the HiRISE area.
  • HiRISE Imagery and Elevation Data: High-resolution photographs and terrain information from NASA's Planetary Data System (PDS) and USGS, supporting detailed terrain visualization and 3D views.

We also use NASA Mars 2020 mission data to represent the Perseverance rover's route, elevation information, and scientific stops, alongside ground photographs from NASA's raw images feed.

These resources allow us to base our project on real Martian geography rather than fictional landscapes.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Mars.loc aims to make planetary navigation easier to understand and support future exploration planning.

By combining interactive mapping, terrain visualization, and navigation information, our platform demonstrates how astronauts could better understand their surroundings and examine potential travel routes.

In the future, Mars.loc could help astronauts identify suitable paths, avoid hazardous terrain, and estimate travel times more accurately.

The project also has educational value, allowing students, researchers, and space enthusiasts to explore real Martian landscapes through an accessible digital platform.

What Makes Mars.loc Creative?

Our innovation is bringing familiar Earth-style navigation concepts to another planet while combining them with real NASA planetary data.

Instead of simply displaying images of Mars, we created an interactive platform that connects geographical information, route visualization, scientific datasets, and 3D terrain exploration.

Our approach combines modern web technologies with planetary science to demonstrate how digital tools could make Mars exploration more understandable and engaging.

We also envision integrating Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR) to provide immersive navigation experiences in future versions.

Current Prototype and Demonstration Features

Mars.loc currently demonstrates several important features:

  1. Interactive 2D Mapping: Users can explore Martian terrain through an interactive map.
  2. 3D Terrain Visualization: Three.js provides the technology for representing Martian terrain in three dimensions.
  3. Route Visualization: The website displays a predefined route representing a proposed safer travel path.
  4. Navigation Information: The platform presents region details, time indicators, and estimated travel duration.
  5. Scientific Data Integration: The project uses real Mars imagery, elevation datasets, and Perseverance rover information.

The displayed route and navigation estimates are currently predefined demonstration values. They are not automatically recalculated or updated in real time.

The prototype also does not yet automatically evaluate terrain hazards to identify the safest possible route.

Factors We Considered

During development, our team focused on astronaut safety, terrain accuracy, usability, accessibility, and future expansion.

We considered the importance of understanding slopes, elevation differences, and natural obstacles when planning travel across Mars.

We also prioritized using reliable planetary data sources and presenting geographical information through an interface that users can understand easily.

Another important consideration was creating a foundation that could support more advanced navigation technologies in the future.

Future Development

Our long-term goal is to transform Mars.loc into an intelligent planetary navigation platform.

We plan to introduce dynamic route calculation, automatic terrain safety analysis, improved travel-time estimates, and more advanced 3D exploration.

We also aim to integrate AR and VR technologies, allowing future astronauts to visualize navigation guidance and explore Martian environments through immersive experiences.

These improvements could make Mars.loc a more useful tool for planning journeys across unfamiliar planetary terrain.

Conclusion

Mars.loc combines real NASA planetary data, modern web development, interactive mapping, and 3D visualization to demonstrate a new approach to Mars navigation.

Although our current platform is a prototype, it establishes a foundation for future navigation tools that could help astronauts understand terrain, evaluate travel routes, and prepare for exploration.

Our vision is to make planetary exploration safer, smarter, and more accessible while inspiring new possibilities for space technology.

Mars.loc – Making the Unknown Easier to Explore.
